proof:
(TH) denotes the frozen statement of the sibling node root.submanifold_tangent-a1 (Submission.simon_submanifold_tangent_basics), taken here as an explicit hypothesis: (TH1) for all n, N, r ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝᴺ and every Simon local representation (V, W, ψ) of M of class r, tangentSpace M (ψ x) = range Dψ(x) for every x ∈ V; (TH2) every n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold M of ℝᴺ is a measurable set and y ↦ tangentProjection M y is continuous on M.
Notation. ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); Hⁿ := μHE[n]. A chart of class r of M is a triple (V, W, ψ) with Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ: V ⊆ ℝⁿ and W ⊆ ℝᴺ open, ψ C^r on V, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ relatively proper (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W) and Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V. For y ∈ M: T_y := tangentSpace M y, P_y := tangentProjection M y (orthogonal projection onto T_y), v^⊥ := normalPart M y v = v − P_y v, τ_i := tangentFrame M y i (an orthonormal basis of T_y), B_y(τ, η) := secondFundamentalForm M y τ η = (fderivWithin ℝ (tangentProjection M) M y τ) η, H(y) := meanCurvature M y = Σ_i B_y(τ_i, τ_i), div_M Y(y) := tangentialDivergence M Y y = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩, and D²ψ(x)[a, b] := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x a b (the derivative at x in direction a of x′ ↦ Dψ(x′)b).

Source: Simon, Ch. 2, Lemma 5.11 (p. 65), with the C³ correction of the README errata (5.4 and 5.11 use deformations of class C³). Printed proof: "First we note that ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0 by virtue of the fact that M is stationary in U, and div_M X = −X · H = 0 by virtue of 4.29 and 5.5(2) and the fact that X is normal to M. The proof is then completed by noting that τ_i · D_{τ_j}X = −X · B(τ_i, τ_j) by virtue of 4.24 and the fact that X is normal to M." The detailed argument below is parent proof II.3 (steps 8-12); the localisation of parent step 9 is replaced by the sibling stationary_mean_zero, which proves "stationary ⇒ H = 0 on M ∩ U" for arbitrary open U by the same argument (parent II.2 steps 6-7).

Setting. Assume (TH), FirstVariation and SecondVariation. Unfold SecondVariationStationary: let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, M, U, K ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and φ : ℝ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ^{n+ℓ} with M an n-dimensional C² Simon submanifold, U open, (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅, IsStationaryIn n M U, IsAdmissibleDeformation 3 U K φ, and X := initialVelocity φ normal to M: ⟨X(y), v⟩ = 0 for y ∈ M, v ∈ T_y. Let Z := initialAcceleration φ, A := deformedArea n M K φ, τ_i := tangentFrame M y i, B_y := secondFundamentalForm M y, H := meanCurvature M, Hⁿ := μHE[n].

1. (Regularity.) K is compact and K ⊆ U. By sibling deformation_regularity (second conjunct), X is C² and Z is C¹ on ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and X = Z = 0 off K. Since Kᶜ is open, X and Z vanish on a neighbourhood of every y ∉ K, so DX(y) = DZ(y) = 0 for y ∉ K.
2. (Compactness and finiteness.) M ∩ K is compact: if y_k ∈ M ∩ K and y_k → y, then y ∈ K ⊆ U (K is closed) and y ∈ closure M; since (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅, y ∈ M. So M ∩ K is a closed subset of the compact set K. By the first conjunct of IsStationaryIn, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞.
3. (H = 0 on M ∩ U.) By sibling stationary_mean_zero (hypotheses (TH), FirstVariation, M C², U open, M stationary in U), H(y) = 0 for every y ∈ M ∩ U.
4. (∫_M div_M Z = 0.) By sibling divergence_identity (Y := Z ∈ C¹, S := K closed, Z = 0 off K, M ∩ K compact), div_M Z is integrable on M and ∫_M div_M Z = −∫_M ⟨Z, H⟩. For y ∈ M, ⟨Z(y), H(y)⟩ = 0 (if y ∈ U, H(y) = 0 by step 3; if y ∉ U, then y ∉ K and Z(y) = 0). Hence ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0. (This is the printed "∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ = 0 by virtue of the fact that M is stationary in U".)
5. (Pointwise identity.) For every y ∈ M: secondVariationIntegrand M φ y = div_M Z(y) + stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ y.
 (a) y ∈ M ∖ K: X(y) = 0, DX(y) = 0 and DZ(y) = 0 (step 1), so div_M Z(y) = 0, div_M X(y) = 0, normalPart M y (DX(y) τ_i) = 0, ⟨τ_i, DX(y) τ_j⟩ = 0 and ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩ = 0 for all i, j; both sides are 0.
 (b) y ∈ M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ U: X is differentiable at y (C²) and normal along M, so by sibling sff_properties (third conjunct), for all i, j: (**) ⟨τ_j, DX(y) τ_i⟩ = −⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩. [(**) actually holds at every y ∈ M, since X is C² everywhere and normal along M; the case split (a)/(b) is only used to know H(y) = 0, which needs y ∈ U.] Hence div_M X(y) = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DX(y) τ_i⟩ = −⟨X(y), Σ_i B_y(τ_i, τ_i)⟩ = −⟨X(y), H(y)⟩ = 0 by step 3 (the printed "div_M X = −X · H = 0"). Using (**) twice and the symmetry B_y(τ_j, τ_i) = B_y(τ_i, τ_j) (sff_properties, first conjunct): ⟨τ_i, DX(y) τ_j⟩ ⟨τ_j, DX(y) τ_i⟩ = ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_j, τ_i)⟩ ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩ = ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩² (the printed "τ_i · D_{τ_j}X = −X · B(τ_i, τ_j)"). Substituting into secondVariationIntegrand = div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i |(DX τ_i)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j} ⟨τ_i, DX τ_j⟩⟨τ_j, DX τ_i⟩ gives div_M Z(y) + Σ_i |(DX(y) τ_i)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j} ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩² = div_M Z(y) + stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ y.
6. (Integrability of the stable integrand.) For y ∈ M let F(y) := trace(P_y DX(y)* (I − P_y) DX(y) P_y) − trace(P_y DX(y)* P_y DX(y) P_y). For any orthonormal basis (τ_i) of T_y and linear L, Σ_i ⟨τ_i, L τ_i⟩ = trace(P_y L P_y). Hence Σ_i ‖(DX(y) τ_i)^⊥‖² = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DX(y)* (I − P_y) DX(y) τ_i⟩ (I − P_y is a self-adjoint idempotent) = trace(P_y DX(y)* (I − P_y) DX(y) P_y); and, by (**) for y ∈ M ∩ K and trivially for y ∈ M ∖ K (both sides 0), Σ_{i,j} ⟨X(y), B_y(τ_i, τ_j)⟩² = Σ_{i,j} ⟨τ_j, DX(y) τ_i⟩² = Σ_i ‖P_y DX(y) τ_i‖² = trace(P_y DX(y)* P_y DX(y) P_y). So stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ = F on M. F is continuous on M (y ↦ P_y is continuous on M by (TH2), DX is continuous, and adjoint, composition and trace are continuous), so the stable integrand is continuous on M and a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ restricted to M (M is measurable by (TH2)). It vanishes on M ∖ K (5(a)) and is bounded on the compact set M ∩ K; as Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ (step 2), it is integrable on M.
7. (Integral identity.) By step 5 (equality on the measurable set M; setIntegral_congr_fun), the integrability of div_M Z (step 4) and of the stable integrand (step 6), and additivity of the integral: ∫_M secondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ = ∫_M div_M Z dHⁿ + ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ = ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ by step 4.
8. (Case U ∩ M ≠ ∅.) SecondVariation applies: M is a C¹ Simon submanifold (each class-2 chart is a class-1 chart); U is open; U ∩ M ≠ ∅; μHE[n](K′ ∩ M) = μHE[n](M ∩ K′) < ∞ for every compact K′ ⊆ U by IsStationaryIn; φ is admissible of class 3. It yields (∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, DifferentiableAt ℝ A t) and HasDerivAt (deriv A) (∫_M secondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ) 0, and by step 7 the value equals ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ.
9. (Case U ∩ M = ∅.) Then M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ U = ∅, so A(t) = (Hⁿ(φ t '' ∅)).toReal = 0 for every t: A is the zero function, differentiable everywhere, deriv A is the zero function, and HasDerivAt (deriv A) 0 0. Every y ∈ M lies outside U ⊇ K, so by 5(a) the stable integrand vanishes on M and ∫_M stableSecondVariationIntegrand M φ dHⁿ = 0. Hence the conclusion holds in this case too.
10. Steps 8 and 9 prove SecondVariationStationary.
key_steps: X ∈ C², Z ∈ C¹ vanish (with derivatives) off K (deformation_regularity); M ∩ K is compact since (closure M ∖ M) ∩ U = ∅; H = 0 on M ∩ U (stationary_mean_zero).
Normal-field identity ⟨τ_j,DXτ_i⟩ = −⟨X,B(τ_i,τ_j)⟩ and symmetry of B (sff_properties): div_M X = −⟨X,H⟩ = 0 and secondVariationIntegrand = div_M Z + stableSecondVariationIntegrand on M.
The stable integrand equals a continuous trace expression on M, hence is integrable; SecondVariation (or the trivial case U ∩ M = ∅) gives the result.
